comment: Corrections to HydroLAKES' modelled mean depth, by lake.
Depth_avg is modelled from a volume estimate, not measured, and it is wrong
for some lakes by an order of magnitude. Since a lake's tone is read off its
mean depth, a wrong value shows as a lake of visibly the wrong colour beside
its neighbours -- which is how the first entry here was found.
1. Match it by 'name', exactly as HydroLAKES spells it (the viewer's popup
2. Give 'depth_avg_m' and cite where the figure comes from in 'source'.
3. Republish the viewer. No archive needs rebuilding: the lake fill reads
depth at draw time, and the bed archive is keyed on surface elevation.
Rebuild the flat tile tree only when one is next rendered.
depth_avg_m   the corrected mean depth, in metres
source        where the figure comes from, for the next reader

lakes.name: Kara-Bogaz-Gol Gulf
lakes.source: Evaporation basin off the Caspian; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garabogazkol gives a mean of about 10 m. HydroLAKES records 101.

lakes.name: Neuchatel
lakes.source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Neuchatel gives a mean of 64.2 m. HydroLAKES records 18.7, which drew it pale beside Geneva and made Geneva look unduly dark by contrast.
